subject: Risk & Compliance
title: A Brief History of Codes
description: A fast breakdown of A Brief History of Codes for builders.

hook.text: The Hippocratic Oath dates to 400 BC. It was the first professional code of conduct: 'First, do no harm.'

buildup.text: Professional codes spread from medicine to law, engineering, and eventually corporate business.

discovery.text: After Enron's collapse in 2001, Sarbanes-Oxley required public companies to adopt and disclose codes of ethics.

twist.text: Enron had a 64-page code of ethics. The board suspended it twice to approve deals that eventually destroyed the company.

climax.text: Codes matter only if enforced. A code on paper that leadership ignores is worse than having no code at all.

punchline.text: Enron had a 64-page code. They suspended it. Twice.

quiz.question: What happened with Enron's code of ethics?
options: The board suspended it twice to approve risky deals
It was the gold standard for corporate ethics
